purpose: Every live public-schema object on canonical staging is either defined by this repository's executable lineage or held under an explicit exception recorded here. Staging only; no production authority.

reverse_lineage_check.method: Strict reverse check over a read-only catalogue capture: an object is explained only by a DEFINING statement in database/migrations Up sections (never-apply files excluded) or the bootstrap snapshot supabase_schema.sql — CREATE/RENAME for relations, functions, triggers, policies and indexes; CREATE TABLE column lists, ADD/RENAME COLUMN; CONSTRAINT/ADD CONSTRAINT or PostgreSQL's automatic name for an inline constraint of a lineage table; serial sequences and constraint indexes by catalogue ownership; dynamic EXECUTE format() builders only where the builder statement and its literal iteration list name the object exactly (013 + 20260905090000 platform-admin policies, 013/20260727120000/20260731100000 updated_at triggers, 20260817140000 trust-cache columns and index, 20260818110000 source-vocabulary constraints).

constraints.identity_biometric_consent_actor: CHECK ((((actor_kind = 'user'::text) AND (actor_user_id IS NOT NULL)) OR (actor_kind = 'system'::text)))
constraints.identity_biometric_consents_user_id_fkey: FOREIGN KEY (user_id) REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE

live_footprint.trigger: CREATE TRIGGER trg_identity_biometric_consents_append_only BEFORE DELETE OR UPDATE ON public.identity_biometric_consents FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION identity_biometric_consents_append_only()

exceptions.equivalence_to_candidate: Every live object matches the candidate definitions: 14 columns, 6 constraints (incl. user_id ON DELETE CASCADE), 2 indexes, the append-only trigger, the function body (md5 equal), RLS enabled+forced, grants postgres+service_role only; the 8 assessment columns (numeric(5,4) scores) and 2 indexes.

unresolved_before_promotion.question: identity_biometric_consents.user_id is ON DELETE CASCADE (candidate and live) while the X3 identity-history ledger uses RESTRICT: which retention/erasure rule governs biometric consent history?
unresolved_before_promotion.observed_behaviour: Proven on disposable PostgreSQL 17.11 with the candidate SQL: because the BEFORE DELETE append-only trigger also fires for the cascaded delete, deleting a user who has consent rows FAILS ('identity_biometric_consents is append-only: DELETE is not permitted') and both rows survive. CASCADE therefore neither erases nor cleanly restricts — it blocks erasure with a trigger error.
requires: selected biometric provider + signed data-processor agreement
unresolved_before_promotion.blocks: promotion of the candidates and any consent/assessment service
